create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

metadata.documented_via: Manage users and webhook event mapping
Manage users and webhook event mapping

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to an existing Logto user when the working email matches an existing account.
oidc_jwt.note: Different upstream identities sharing the same email may intentionally merge; use distinct emails for collision tests.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct_sign_in references a missing or disabled connector, Logto redirects the user to the standard sign-in page instead of hard-failing the request.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat fallback to hosted sign-in as a flow-coherence bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs keep their old scopes until expiration even after role or permission changes; only newly issued tokens reflect updates.
oidc_jwt.note: Use newly issued tokens when testing permission tightening or enlargement.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT; this token is meant for /oidc/me and introspection.
oidc_jwt.note: Lack of JWT claims in this case is by design, not a token-format bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization tokens are not returned directly from the authorization code flow; they must be obtained via refresh token flow or client credentials with organization parameters.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag absence of organization token in direct code exchange as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs keep old scopes after permission changes; only newly issued tokens reflect updates.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag unchanged old JWT contents after role changes as stale-cache vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted permissions do not appear through refresh unless already within the original requested scope set.
oidc_jwt.note: A missing newly granted scope after refresh can be by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Ending the Logto session does not revoke grants with offline_access by default; refresh capability may remain until grant expiration.
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout refresh success can be by design when offline_access was granted.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer access tokens are validated statelessly; repeated use of the same JWT is not prevented by default.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report lack of jti replay tracking for ordinary JWT API access as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.constraint: When testing I2 expired_token or future_token against Logto-issued JWTs, include a CONTROL token request that should succeed (for example a normal authorization_code, refresh_token, or client_credentials request for the same client/resource). Without a control, a token failure may be caused by missing resource, missing organization_id, disabled grant type, or missing role assignment rather than time validation.

The /oidc/token endpoint uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests. The fuzzer MUST send form-encoded bodies, not JSON, for authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, and token_exchange requests.
oidc_jwt.source: core service OIDC provider docs; personal access token docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience-binding tests on global API resources, the resource parameter MUST exactly match the registered API identifier URI. Logto does exact matching; prefixes, shortened names, or approximate values do not match.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, remember Logto issues an opaque access token when no resource is specified in the authorization request, except when a default API resource is configured. To test JWT audience enforcement, request a specific resource or ensure a default API resource is configured; otherwise failures/successes may reflect opaque-token behavior instead of JWT aud validation.

If a default API resource is configured, omitting resource does not mean 'no audience restriction': Logto will use the default API resource as the audience for tokens. I5 empty_audience tests MUST account for this by distinguishing 'resource omitted with default API configured' from 'resource omitted with no default API'.

For organization-level API or organization-permission tests, organization RBAC is only applied when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. The fuzzer MUST include organization_id when testing organization context binding.

Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. To obtain an organization token after interactive login, the fuzzer MUST use the refresh_token flow with organization parameters, or use client_credentials for M2M scenarios.

For I5 scope-escalation and permission-change tests, Logto enforces a scope subset rule: a newly issued access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. The fuzzer MUST request the superset of scopes up front if later refresh-based comparisons need to observe narrowing; otherwise missing scopes may be due to original-request limits, not authorization enforcement.

For global API resources, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh if they were not part of the original request set; a new OAuth authorization flow is required. Therefore I3 config-change tests that expect broadened scopes after admin changes MUST use a fresh authorization flow, not only refresh.

For downscoping tests, existing JWTs keep old scopes until they expire. A valid I3/I5 test must compare a newly issued token after the config or role change, not reuse an old JWT and expect its claims to mutate.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running RFC 8693 tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled; otherwise failures are expected and are not evidence of correct audience/scope enforcement.

For token_exchange tests, Logto uses the same /oidc/token endpoint as other grants. The fuzzer MUST set grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and provide the correct subject_token_type. For PAT exchange specifically, subject_token_type must be urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use the resource parameter as the requested target audience at /oidc/token. The docs describe resource indicators, not a separate audience field, for Logto token issuance. Supplying only a nonstandard audience parameter may not exercise the intended binding logic.

For I1 signing-key-rotation coherence tests, Logto signing key rotation changes the JWKS immediately in Cloud, but rotating keys consecutively can invalidate all issued tokens. The fuzzer MUST perform at most one rotation per test sequence and compare old-token rejection only after a single controlled rotation.

For OSS deployments, after rotating signing keys a Logto instance restart is required for the new signing key to take effect. I3 key-rotation tests on OSS MUST include a restart step or avoid asserting immediate propagation.
Logto userinfo is mounted at /oidc/me, not /userinfo. The fuzzer MUST use /oidc/me for verify_granted_identity on this platform.

Opaque tokens are intended for /oidc/me and introspection-based validation. If the fuzzer needs JWT claim inspection or audience enforcement tests, it MUST obtain a JWT by requesting a specific resource or organization token; using an opaque token will not expose JWT claims and can cause false positives.

For I5 organization token tests, organization permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in a single token model. The fuzzer MUST not interpret rejection of mixed-scope requests as a bug; instead test global and organization permission models separately.

For I4 cross-provider or cross-connector identity tests involving enterprise/social sign-in, Logto may automatically link identities to an existing user when the email matches. The fuzzer MUST treat email-based auto-linking as by-design and use distinct emails when testing whether different upstream principals collapse unexpectedly.

For I4 case-confusion tests on usernames, Logto has a deployment-level CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME setting. The fuzzer MUST record whether usernames are case-sensitive in the target deployment before interpreting Admin vs admin results as a collision or separation bug.

For direct sign-in tests, if the specified connector is not found or not enabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page. The fuzzer MUST detect this fallback and not misclassify it as successful direct provider binding.

For sign-out or session-revocation tests, Logto signOut/end-session clears the centralized Logto session, but grants with offline_access may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. The fuzzer MUST not assume end-session revokes all refresh-token capability when offline_access was granted.

Grant lifetime default is 180 days, and offline_access grants can survive end-session. Freshness tests that expect immediate invalidation after logout MUST use explicit token revocation or avoid offline_access, otherwise continued refresh may be by design.

For I5 scope matching, Logto permission names are exact strings. There is no wildcard or prefix matching for requested scopes such as read vs read:elections. Multi-permission tests MUST request the exact permission names defined on the API resource.

When testing JWT-based API access against Logto, the client MUST request a resource indicator (`resource`) if it expects a JWT access token for an API. If no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
When using `verify_granted_identity`, the fuzzer MUST account for Logto's nonstandard UserInfo path: the OIDC UserInfo endpoint is mounted at `/oidc/me`, not the more common `/userinfo`.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the verifier MUST check `iss` against `https://<tenant>/oidc` exactly. Documentation states issuer is fixed and not customizable; forged or alternate issuer values must be rejected.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST request and validate the exact API resource indicator URI. Logto requires the `resource` parameter to exactly match the registered API identifier; there is no wildcard or prefix matching.
For I5 scope-binding tests, requested scope names MUST exactly match the permission names defined for the API resource. Prefixes, shortened names, or wildcard-like partial values do not match.

For I2 expired-token and future-token tests, include a control token minted under the same tenant and resource settings. A failed attack token without a valid control cannot distinguish claim-time rejection from wrong audience/resource setup.

For organization-token tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT expect organization tokens directly from the initial authorization code exchange. Documentation states Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow; use refresh_token or client_credentials with `organization_id`.
For I5 organization authorization tests, organization RBAC is only applied when `organization_id` is included in the token request. If omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated.

For I5 organization-level API tests, the token request MUST include both `resource` and `organization_id`. Without `organization_id`, organization RBAC is not enforced; without `resource`, the token shape/audience differs.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are BY DESIGN not modified after role/permission changes. Only newly issued tokens reflect reduced scopes immediately; tests must compare fresh token issuance behavior, not expect old JWTs to mutate.

For I3 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, refresh alone will NOT add newly granted scopes unless they were part of the original authorization request subset. To test newly granted scopes, run a new authorization flow.

For I3 organization-token enlarged-permission tests, new permissions can appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but still only within the originally requested scope set. Do not interpret missing newly granted scopes outside the original request as a bug.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any `token_exchange` test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected and not security findings.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, use the token endpoint `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`. PAT exchange and impersonation exchange both use this same endpoint and are audience/resource-bound by the request.

For I2 replay_same_token against ordinary JWT bearer access to APIs, replay is BY DESIGN for stateless JWT validation unless the context is one-time subject tokens. Do not flag repeated use of the same JWT access token as a vulnerability by itself.

For one-time impersonation subject tokens, replay expectations differ: documentation states the subject token is short-lived and one-time-use. Replay tests should target subject-token exchange, not ordinary JWT API access.

For I3 signing-key-rotation tests, avoid consecutive rotations. Documentation warns that rotating signing keys two or more times consecutively may invalidate all issued tokens; such failures are by design and not evidence of stale trust.

For Cloud tenants, signing key rotation takes effect immediately; for OSS, instance restart is required after rotation. I3 key-rotation tests must account for deployment mode or they will misclassify propagation timing.

For sign-out or revocation freshness tests, revoking a token via `/oidc/token/revocation` is distinct from ending the centralized Logto browser session. Client-side sign-out or end-session may leave grants alive when `offline_access` was granted.

For I2 logout freshness tests involving refresh tokens, note that if `offline_access` is granted, end-session does not revoke that app grant by default. Refresh-token usability after browser logout may be by design until grant expiry or explicit revocation.

Default API resource behavior affects token format. If a default API resource is configured and `resource` is omitted, Logto may use that default audience; additionally, if `openid` is included with no resource, Logto issues an opaque access token for UserInfo. Tests must control both `resource` and `openid` to avoid false positives.
For direct sign-in tests using `direct_sign_in`, failure to find or enable the connector falls back to the standard sign-in page by design. Do not treat fallback as a flow-confusion vulnerability.

For OIDC request-object tests (`request` parameter on `/oidc/auth`), the docs only document support for passing a request object but do not specify request-object signature policy. The fuzzer SHOULD explicitly test unsigned and attacker-signed request objects and interpret acceptance carefully as an empirical result, not a documented guarantee.

For I4 identity-linking tests involving enterprise SSO, Logto automatically links enterprise SSO identities to existing users when the working email matches. Different upstream identities collapsing into one downstream account on matching email is documented behavior, not necessarily a principal-binding bug.

For I4 enterprise SSO tests, once an email domain is associated with an enterprise SSO connector, existing users with that domain are restricted to sign in with that enterprise SSO connector and previous sign-in methods are blocked. Authentication-method changes under this condition are by design.

For I4 social/connector identity tests, connector `target` values determine identity-provider naming semantics. Using different connectors with the same target can cause account-linking outcomes; using the same IdP with different targets can intentionally split accounts. Multi-connector collision tests must control connector target configuration.

For I2 replay_same_token on oidc_jwt, DO NOT flag reuse of the same JWT access token as a vulnerability by itself. The docs describe JWT access tokens as bearer tokens and do not document jti replay tracking; stateless JWT reuse is expected behavior unless testing a one-time subject token context such as impersonation subject tokens.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL token flow that should succeed under the same tenant and client configuration. Use valid timing claims such as exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} for the control. Without a control, a 401 on the attack token may reflect wrong issuer, audience, or resource setup rather than freshness enforcement.

The resource parameter is exact-match only. Documentation states the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator). For I5 audience tests, do not use wildcard or prefix assumptions; use the exact registered URI or omit resource entirely when intentionally testing default-resource behavior.

Scope names are exact-match only. Documentation explicitly says prefixes and shortened versions do not work as wildcards. For I5 authorization-binding tests, request the exact permission names defined on the API resource; do not use partial names like 'read' to match 'read:elections'.

When testing I5 empty_audience or missing resource behavior, account for Logto's token format split: if no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. Opaque tokens are for /oidc/me and introspection, not JWT audience validation tests. To test oidc_jwt invariants, request a specific resource or use a configured default API resource that yields JWT access tokens.

Default API resource changes semantics when resource is omitted. If a default API resource is configured, omitting resource can still produce a JWT for that default audience; if openid is included and no resource is present, Logto may issue an opaque token for userinfo. I5 tests that rely on 'missing resource means no audience restriction' must first determine whether a default API resource is configured.

For I5 organization-bound tests, organization RBAC is only applied when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. Do not interpret acceptance without organization_id as an org-bound authorization bypass.

Organization permissions and global API permissions are distinct and cannot be mixed in one authorization model. For I5 tests, do not request organization permissions and expect them to satisfy global API resource checks, or vice versa.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are BY DESIGN not modified after issuance. Documentation states permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. A valid I3 test must compare newly issued tokens before and after config change, not expect an already-issued JWT to shrink immediately.

For I3 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, refresh does NOT add newly granted scopes unless they were part of the original authorization request set; a new authorization flow is required. Do not treat absence of newly granted scopes after refresh as a bug.

For I3 downscoping tests, newly issued tokens should reflect reduced scopes immediately, but existing JWTs may continue to work until expiration. Use short-lived tokens or force a new issuance when validating permission tightening.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running any RFC 8693 token_exchange tests, enable 'Allow token exchange' on the target application; otherwise failures are expected and not evidence of correct audience or scope enforcement.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation and related token exchange tests, remember that PAT-exchanged access tokens are documented to behave identically to refresh-token-issued access tokens. Differences in claims or permissions between those two paths would be security-relevant; similarity is by design.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and explicit resource or audience parameters as documented. Do not test against /oidc/token/introspection or /oidc/me; those endpoints validate different semantics.

For I4 identity-binding tests using enterprise SSO or social/connector-backed identities, Logto may auto-link a new external identity to an existing user when the email matches. This is documented behavior. To avoid false positives, use distinct emails when you need separate downstream identities, or explicitly classify same-email linking as by design.

Username case sensitivity is deployment-configurable via CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME and defaults to true. For I4 case_confusion tests, do not assume case folding unless the deployment is known to disable case sensitivity.

For I4 cross-provider or cross-connector identity tests, connector target values influence account linking semantics. Different connectors with the same target can collapse identities; same IdP with different targets can intentionally create separate accounts. Do not interpret these documented connector-target behaviors as unexpected identity collisions.

For I1 issuer-validation tests in relying-party style verification, issuer must be checked against the tenant issuer from discovery or the fixed /oidc issuer URL. The docs repeatedly show verify_iss=true / issuer=ISSUER while audience may be verified manually. A test that omits issuer validation is not a valid proof-integrity test.

For I1 audience-validation tests, many Logto examples intentionally disable library-level audience verification (verify_aud=false) and require manual audience checks based on permission model. A backend that accepts a token after only signature+issuer validation is misconfigured application code, not necessarily a Logto broker flaw. Distinguish platform behavior from relying-party sample behavior.

For I2 and I3 sign-out/revocation tests, end-session and token revocation are not equivalent. End-session clears the centralized Logto session, but grants with offline_access may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. Do not expect global sign-out alone to invalidate all refresh-token-derived authorization immediately.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time has a documented default of 3600 seconds when not set. Missing value means platform default, not zero. Do not assume omitted expiry disables expiration or creates a zero-second token.
Numeric sentinel analysis: one-time token (magic link) expiresIn defaults to 10 minutes when not specified. Omitted expiresIn selects a nonzero default rather than disabling expiry.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
